summary.text: Tom Barrett is the Republican incumbent, seeking a second term representing Michigan's 7th District. A 22-year U.S. Army veteran and helicopter pilot, he served four years in the Michigan House and four in the Michigan Senate before winning the congressional seat in 2024 on his second attempt. According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he is running on housing and health care costs and on setting clear limits on military deployments.

paragraphs.text: Tom Barrett is a lifelong Michigan resident who, according to his official biography, grew up in a family where his father worked two jobs and his mother stayed home to raise Tom and his six siblings.

He served in the U.S. Army from 2000 to 2022, including during Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Iraqi Freedom, and reached the rank of Chief Warrant Officer. A helicopter pilot in the Michigan Army National Guard, he lists service in Iraq, Guantanamo Bay, Kuwait and the Korean DMZ and more than 1,000 flight hours.
Barrett graduated from Western Michigan University with honors in 2007 through the Montgomery GI Bill, according to his official biography.
Barrett was elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (District 71) and served from 2015 to 2019, chairing the Military and Veterans Affairs Committee in the 2015 session.
He won election to the Michigan Senate (District 24) in 2018 and served until 2023, chairing the Senate Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.
In 2022 he ran for Congress and lost to Rep. Elissa Slotkin (D), 51.7% to 46.3%.
Barrett won Michigan's 7th District in November 2024, defeating Curtis Hertel (D) 50.3% to 46.6%, and took office in 2025 as Slotkin's successor.

In the U.S. House he serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and the Veterans' Affairs Committee and, according to his Ballotpedia survey, chairs the Technology Modernization Subcommittee.
He lives in Charlotte, Michigan, with his wife, Ashley, and their four children, according to his official biography.
